subject.title: [Bug]: gateway.nodes.denyCommands silently accepts invalid command names without warning

question: Should `gateway.nodes.denyCommands` write-time validation warn only, fail closed, or remain audit-only when entries are unknown to the current command registry?
rationale: This is a security boundary and compatibility choice: warning-only reduces false confidence without blocking custom/plugin commands, while fail-closed behavior could break valid operator setups.

options.title: Warn on config write
options.body: Emit actionable warnings for unknown or pattern-like entries during `config set` and keep audit-time findings for later checks.

options.title: Fail closed on unknowns
options.body: Reject unknown deny entries at write time, but require explicit compatibility handling for plugin and custom command IDs.

options.title: Keep audit-only
options.body: Leave config writes free-form and rely on `openclaw security audit` to catch ineffective entries after the fact.

recommendation.title: Warn on config write
recommendation.body: Emit actionable warnings for unknown or pattern-like entries during `config set` and keep audit-time findings for later checks.

likelyOwner.reason: The current schema, node command policy, and audit hardening history all point to this area ownership trail.
